claim: On cued-solved problems, m21 answers that open deliberatively are right at about the cued base's rate and the others at about the plain base's rate, a gap G in [0.20, 0.65].

The 1.5x edit carries RL's re-ranking of routes, so where both fail its normalized wrong-answer agreement with RL exceeds the cued base's by 0.08-0.6.

The 1.5x top-8 edit shares RL's route re-ranking, so on fresh2026 problems where edit, RL and cued base all fail, the edit's wrong answers are closer to RL's than the base's are after normalizing each model's own concentration (D_fresh in [0.08, 0.6]).
The edit has no route preference beyond fewer slips, so its normalized wrong-answer agreement with RL on fresh2026 is no higher than the cued base's (D_fresh in [-0.10, 0.07]).

By step 100 the hold-on shift is partly in the weights, so a step-100 plain sample that does not open deliberatively is right more often than the plain base T3 answer on the same problem, by less than the full cue gain (D in [0.10, 0.38]).
At RL step 100 the plain samples that do not open deliberatively are unswitched plain-base answers, so on the same problem the cued step-100 model is right far more often than they are.
